entries.title: Families call for criminal charges for South Chicago Chapel owners at vigil
entries.summary: <p>Cecelia Palmer was in charge of her sister-in-law’s funeral arrangements earlier this year. Now, she looks back and agonizes about her decision.</p><p>Palmer’s sister-in-law Nicole Williams-Smith was supposedly cremated after her services at South Chicago Chapel, but when her family received the ashes, Palmer said it looked more like a pile of dirt and rocks.</p><p>“What are these?” Palmer said, looking at a photo of the alleged ashes the funeral home gave her. “Are they even human remains?”</p><p>Palmer is now joining the growing number of loved ones demanding answers from the funeral home and city and state officials about what actually happened the remains of their deceased friends and family. Around 25 people gathered at a vigil Sunday evening at the South Chicago Chapel to release balloons and call for criminal charges in the case.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-dd0000" name="image-dd0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f4bb411/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8400x4714+0+443/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe2%2F28%2Ff89cf335465f81b699edcffda8fa%2Fsouth-chi-chapel-vigil-5.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/44a8bbf/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8400x4714+0+443/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe2%2F28%2Ff89cf335465f81b699edcffda8fa%2Fsouth-chi-chapel-vigil-5.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a40f139/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8400x4714+0+443/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe2%2F28%2Ff89cf335465f81b699edcffda8fa%2Fsouth-chi-chapel-vigil-5.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Cecelia Palmer, Nicole Williams-Smith's sister-in-law, was among the relatives and supporters attending a vigil Sunday outside South Chicago Chapel, where dozens of decomposing bodies and unidentified remains were found earlier this month. The funeral home was shut down. Palmer said when she received her sister-in-law's remains, she questioned whether that's what they reallty were - they looked like rocks, she said." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a40f139/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8400x4714+0+443/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe2%2F28%2Ff89cf335465f81b699edcffda8fa%2Fsouth-chi-chapel-vigil-5.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a864c81/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8400x4714+0+443/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe2%2F28%2Ff89cf335465f81b699edcffda8fa%2Fsouth-chi-chapel-vigil-5.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a40f139/2147483647/strip/true/crop/8400x4714+0+443/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe2%2F28%2Ff89cf335465f81b699edcffda8fa%2Fsouth-chi-chapel-vigil-5.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Cecelia Palmer, who was among those attending the vigil Sunday, shows a picture on her phone of the remains of her sister-in-law Nicole Williams-Smith, which she received from South Chicago Chapel. She questioned whether that’s what they really were — they looked like rocks, she said.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Pat Nabong/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“Please, city officials, please step up and do your job,” said Lisette Guillen, executive director of Case Files Chicago. “We need criminal charges on this matter because this behavior is horrific and criminal.”</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/08/06/decomposing-bodies-found-funeral-home-south-chicago-chapel-95th-street" target="_blank" ><u>state shut down</u></a> South Chicago Chapel earlier this month after receiving a tip that owners Clark and Johanna Morgan were improperly storing bodies. Inside the funeral home, investigators found 56 bodies in various stages of decomposition. For months neighbors complained about the smell coming from the building.</p><p>“Was she among those?” Palmer said. “I’ve called and left messages with everybody, emails, so far haven’t heard.”</p><p>It <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago/2026/08/07/owners-of-far-south-side-funeral-home-have-history-of-mishandling-human-remains" target="_blank" ><u>wasn’t the first time</u></a> the couple was accused of mishandling remains. Last year, a Chicago Heights Crematory owned by the Morgans was shut down.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a entries.title: The anatomy of Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong's potential MVP season
entries.summary: <p>As hot as Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is, it’s easy to forget how cold he was.</p><p>Through 50 games, Crow-Armstrong was hitting .225 with an OPS of .659. He had five home runs and 20 RBI. The Cubs were halfway through what became a 10-game losing streak, and manager Craig Counsell was looking for answers.</p><p>After Crow-Armstrong homered in the next game, Counsell moved him from the bottom of the order to the top — the very top.</p><p>“When we moved Pete there, honestly, we needed a jump,” Counsell said. “We were struggling scoring runs, and we were looking for a spark. It wasn’t very analytical. Now I look at the lineup, and he just comes around more.”</p><p>Slowly but surely, Crow-Armstrong began to produce. He got hot in June, hitting 10 home runs in the first 18 games of the month. But it wasn’t until the Cubs’ trip that month to New York to face the Mets that Crow-Armstrong’s season completely changed.</p><p>The way bench coach Ryan Flaherty tells it, Crow-Armstrong was working in the batting cage at Citi Field with assistant hitting coach John Mallee. After his eighth swing, Crow-Armstrong walked out of the cage and essentially said, “I found something that I’m going to be able to repeat for a long time.”</p><p>“He’s a pretty honest kid,” Flaherty told the Sun-Times. “And here we are, two months after that, and he was right on.”</p><p>Entering the game Sunday night against the Reds, Crow-Armstrong was hitting .282 with an OPS of .944, 36 homers — to which he added a leadoff blast Sunday — and 90 RBI. According to wins above replacement, he was the most valuable player in baseball, with marks of 9.1 from Fangraphs and 8.3 from Baseball Reference.</p><p>And he’s the odds-on favorite to win the National League Most Valuable Player Award.</p><p>What the heck happened?</p><p>“It’s just the natural progression of a season,” Crow-Armstrong told the Sun-Times. “I’ve known that I’m capable of this. Obviously, there’s swing changes you can make. I definitely freed myself up by lowering the hands and creating a different kind of rhythm for myself and then implementing the leg kick.</p><p>“Getting on the dish against lefties really helped me learn the strike zone better. But then not feeling like I’m in any rush to get to two strikes. Once I’m there, I still feel like I can control the zone while also looking to do damage.”</p><p>Just last year, Crow-Armstrong occasionally would bunt with two strikes to try to make something happen. Now, 10 of his 37 homers have come with two strikes. Everyone knew he was a defensive phenom, thanks to his speed and athleticism. But the extent of his power has surprised most — but not him.</p><p>“That’s another thing that I’ve always had in me,” he said. “Even when I was in high school, I was kind of slappy, could go the other way really well. I just didn’t know how to pull the ball efficiently. Some swings I’d take I can remember like, Oh, I’ve got that in me, and then I just wouldn’t be able to translate it to the game.</p><p>“John Mallee made it make sense to me that my swing works in that way and I should take advantage of it. So the goal now is the opposite of who I thought I used to be, which was I want my direction to go to left-center so that when I’m early, I can pull the ball.</p><p>“Nah, man. I’m pulling everything you throw at me. That’s my goal. That’s what has helped me start moving really efficiently.”</p><p>Counsell said he knew Crow-Armstrong would hit home runs. It was just a matter of learning how to do it.</p><p>“He was a very young player to the big leagues,” Counsell said of Crow-Armstrong, who made his big-league debut shortly after turning 21. “It’s hard to be able to get the ball in the air to the pull side and have good pitch discipline. Those are two counter things, really, because you have to hit the ball out front, and that means you have to make a decision a little bit sooner.”</p><p>Crow-Armstrong also is proving you don’t need to be big and burly to put a ball into the bleachers.</p><p>“He’s very wiry strong,” Flaherty said. “Pound for pound, I bet he’s one of the stronger guys on the team. You watch him in the weight room, he’s strong. He looks the way he does, but he has the ability to create an absurd amount of force in a short period of time, which I think is where that power comes from. It’s always been there.”</p><p>And it doesn’t appear to be going anywhere.</p><p>“Every time he’s coming to bat right now, it’s like something special’s about to happen,” Flaherty said. “You think he isn’t going to do it again, and he does it again.”</p>

entries.title: Cubs stand behind Shota Imanaga after he allows three homers in loss to Reds
entries.summary: <p>The Cubs have a Shota Imanaga problem, but they’re not ready to admit it.</p><p>The left-hander allowed three home runs Sunday night in a 7-5 loss to the Reds, marking the sixth time this season he has allowed at least three in a game. That’s a record for a franchise that celebrated its 150th year this weekend.</p><p>“He gave up three homers, and two had men on base,” manager Craig Counsell said. “The math doesn’t really work there as far as having a good start. We know Shota is going to give up some home runs. That’s the nature of his repertoire. Three in a start, that’s too many.”</p><p>At least Imanaga lasted longer than the two innings he pitched in his last start a week before in Seattle. But the Cubs overcame that to win 19-2. They gave themselves a chance against Reds ace Chase Burns, taking a 2-0 lead into the fourth, but the offense was too little, too late.</p><p>Imanaga allowed a three-run homer to Hector Rodriguez (his fourth homer of the season), a solo shot to Dane Myers (his sixth) and a two-run shot to Tyler Stephenson on a pitch out of the strike zone, making it 6-3 in the fifth.</p><p>“The mistake pitches that I can’t throw end up in zones that they’re going to hit,” Imanaga said through a translator. “And here, those swings don’t end up in singles; those end up in home runs. There’s a lot of frustration within myself. But I need to be the one to figure it out.”</p><p>Counsell pushed back on the suggestion that Imanaga’s rotation spot is in jeopardy.</p><p>“He’s not having a bad season,” Counsell said. “He’s having a pretty decent season. I wouldn’t say that at all, no. We need Shota. We need Shota to be good for us. So we have to work at helping him be better.”</p><h3>Davis, Lester get blue jackets</h3><p>Former Cubs catcher Jody Davis and pitcher Jon Lester were inducted into the Cubs’ Hall of Fame and received their blue jackets in pregame ceremonies.</p><p>Davis was a two-time All-Star in eight seasons with the Cubs, including 1984, when the team won the National League East for its first postseason appearance in 39 years.</p><p>Lester also was a two-time All-Star in five full seasons with the Cubs, but his postseason achievement was more notable. He helped the 2016 team end the club’s 108-year World Series-championship drought.</p><h3>Notes</h3><p>The Cubs released 2020 first-round pick (16th overall) and Chicago native Ed Howard from Triple-A Iowa on Saturday. Between Iowa and Double-A Knoxville this season, the shortstop was hitting .168 with a .469 OPS and two homers in 52 games.</p><p>• Right-hander Edward Cabrera (blister on middle finger) is scheduled to begin a rehab assignment Tuesday at Iowa.</p><h3>On deck</h3><p><b>BREWERS AT CUBS</b></p><p><b>Monday:</b> Kyle Harrison (10-3, 2.79 ERA) vs. Clay Holmes (5-6, 2.26), 6:40 p.m., Marquee, 670-AM, 104.3-FM.</p><p><b>Tuesday:</b> Robert Gasser (4-5, 4.59) vs. Matthew Boyd (8-3, 3.99), 6:40 p.m., Marquee, 670-AM, 104.3-FM.</p><p><b>Wednesday:</b> Jacob Misiorowski (14-5, 1.73) vs. David Peterson (7-7, 5.11), 6:40 p.m., Marquee, 670-AM, 104.3-FM.</p><p><b>Thursday:</b> Logan Henderson (9-2, 2.48) vs. Kevin Gausman (8-11, 4.52), 6:15 p.m., Fox 32, 670-AM, 104.3-FM.<br></p>

entries.title: Joel Cory, Chicago voice-over actor whose pipes pitched hundreds of brands in TV commercials, dies at 89
entries.summary: <p></p><p></p><p></p><p>It's good work ... if you can get it.</p><p>And Joel Cory got it, and then some.</p><p>"Joel was among the top three voice-over actors in the country during the heyday of television commercials in the 70s, 80s and 90s," said Bill Brichta, a longtime friend and former advertising executive.</p><p>Mr. Cory was the voice of "Pop," one of the elves in the "Snap, Crackle, Pop" trio of mascots for Rice Krispies cereal; a singing grasshopper pitching Cricket cigarette lighters; “Lefty,” the helping hand of Hamburger Helper; and Sprout, the little green class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Sun-Times archive</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Mr. Cory died July 26 from complications of Parkinson's disease. He was 89.</p><p>His life was as colorful as his voice.</p><p>For two decades beginning in 1974, Mr. Cory dated actress Robyn Douglass, who appeared on the cover of Playboy in 1974 and co-starred in the 1979 cult classic film "Breaking Away."</p><p>The couple owned horses and enjoyed equestrian sports like horse jumping. They lived in a lakefront mansion in Wilmette previously owned by a member of the Wrigley chewing gum family.</p><p>Mr. Cory drove a convertible sports car and, in the age before Bluetooth technology, drew flummoxed looks from fellow motorists wondering if he was talking to himself behind the wheel as he rehearsed lines en route to recording sessions in the Loop.</p><p>"I think he felt extraordinarily grateful for the life he had," Brichta said. "The reality of the business is: One day you're in, and the next day you could be out. But Joel was never really out."</p><p>Mr. Cory told the Sun-Times in 1975: "A cold can be a disaster. If I catch one and it's the wrong day, I can blow a year's salary. Even if you're good and in demand, there's pressure. Nobody's indispensable."</p><p>He knew from experience — a head cold once scuttled what promised to be a career-changing breath mints commercial early in his career.</p><p>For years, he carried a beeper to make sure he could answer job calls quickly.</p><p>"I never wanted a real job," he told the Sun-Times in 1992.</p><p>Mr. Cory was a folk singer in the 50s and 60s before getting into advertising voice-over work.</p><p>He lived in Old Town, busked and sang in coffee shops and bars, first as a solo act — mixing sea shanties with humor — then as part of a duo named "The Outsiders" with George McKelvey.</p><p>The two played colleges and released an album "Cheer Up, Me Lads," in 1962.</p><p>One day, early in his singing career, while sitting in his family kitchen, his father pointed to a Cory brand coffee maker and suggested it as a stage name that would be more distinctive than the common Cohen.</p><p>Mr. Cory was born Joel Cohen on Feb. 2, 1937, and grew up in Rogers Park. His father, Maurice Cohen, was an attorney for the state's unemployment office; his mother, Hannah Cohen, was a homemaker who played the piano and sang to her children.</p><p>His mother died when Mr. Cory was 9, and his father remarried to Ida Abt.</p><p>Mr. Cory graduated from Sullivan High School in 1954, where he picked up a love for music and the arts, and went on to earn an accounting degree, at his father's suggestion, after studying at the University of Illinois and Roosevelt University.</p><p>After more than a decade of trying to make the music thing work, including by co-founding a production company and promoting other artists, Mr. Cory found himself still struggling to make rent.</p><p>"I either had to get into commercials or starve," he told the Chicago Reader in 1977.</p><p>In the early 70s, Mr. Cory met Dick Orkin, a voice actor and radio producer who created "Chickenman," a radio series that spoofed comic book heroes, and "The Secret Adventures of the Tooth Fairy," a radio show about a dental assistant who claimed to be the Tooth Fairy.</p><p>Mr. Cory took on multiple voice actor roles in each radio show, jump-starting his career as a voice-acting talent.</p><p>Mr. Cory, a longtime board member of the Hubbard Street Dance Company, married Katie Cory in 2002 on their favorite ski run at the top of Deer Valley ski resort. The couple spent part of their honeymoon cycling in the Tuscany region of Italy.</p><p>"He would play his guitar and serenade me to sleep at night," his wife said, who added they each referred to one another as "best friends for life."</p><p>Although many people asked, Mr. Cory almost never performed his voice-over characters outside the studio.</p><p>"He wouldn't do it until his grandkids were born, and then he did any character of his they wanted to hear," said his wife.</p><p>Mr. Cory also served in the Army and the Army National Reserves in the 1950s.</p><p>In addition to his wife, Mr. Cory is survived by his daughters, Eve Adair and Ashley Petric Dempsey; his son, Thomas Petric; and five grandchildren.</p>

entries.title: Blue Cross Blue Shield’s 'downcoding' will gravely impact care
entries.summary: <p>Due to Blue Cross Blue Shield’s unfair new "downcoding" scheme the Sun-Times' Elvia Malagón recently <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/08/26/blue-cross-blue-shield-lowers-payment-therapists-pediatricians-new-downcoding-policy" >wrote</a> about, more and more physicians are considering dropping Blue Cross Blue Shield plans or not accepting insurance all together. This could interrupt the relationship thousands of patients in Illinois have with their current doctors or lead them to lose their access to healthcare entirely.</p><p>Our concerns are urgent and real. A growing number of psychiatrists, especially those with small practices lacking the resources to constantly fight the reimbursement bureaucracy, have already stopped accepting insurance entirely and moved to the private pay model. Blue Cross Blue Shield's new push to shortchange providers will force many more to follow suit.</p><p>Blue Cross Blue Shield's position in the face of this potential crisis of its own making has been irresponsible and disappointing. When we wrote and requested a meeting with the president of Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois, all we got back was a generic non-response response “explaining” policy.</p><p>We urge Blue Cross Blue Shield patients to talk to their doctors and psychotherapists about downcoding. Contact your elected officials if you feel your access to healthcare has been diminished because of this situation. And learn how to file a complaint on the <a class="Link" href="https://idoi.illinois.gov/consumers/file-a-complaint.html." target="_blank" >Illinois Department of Insurance</a>'s website.</p><p>If Blue Cross Blue Shield refuses to act fairly, legally and responsibly, it’s time for state and federal regulators to step in and hold them to account.</p><p><i>Dr. Steven Weinstein, president, Illinois Psychiatric Society</i></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-050000" name="module-050000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>Give us your take</h3><br>Send letters to the editor to <a class="Link" href="mailto:letters@suntimes.com" target="_blank" >letters@suntimes.com</a>. To be considered for publication, letters must include your full name, your neighborhood or hometown and a phone number for verification purposes. Letters should be a maximum of approximately 375 words.</div> </div><p></p><h3>Mail-in meddling won’t deter Illinois</h3><p>Recent news<b> </b>about President Donald Trump’s acrimonious battle against <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/08/26/illinois-ag-kwame-raoul-lawsuit-postal-service-mail-ballot-rule-midterm-elections" >mail-in voting</a> has understandably left some voters with questions and concerns about whether the vote by mail rules have changed in Illinois.</p><p>As Cook County clerk and the county’s chief election authority, I want to assure voters: Nothing has changed. Eligible Illinois voters can still choose to vote by mail, and they can have confidence their ballots will be handled securely.</p><p>Voting by mail is not a shortcut around the safeguards that protect our elections. It is a secure, established voting option governed by state law and subject to multiple checks throughout the process.</p><p>When a voter requests a mail ballot, that ballot is sent to the voter’s registered address. Once it is returned, election officials verify the required information before it can be counted. Ballots are securely transported, tracked and processed by trained election personnel. These procedures are designed to protect the integrity of every ballot while ensuring that every eligible voter can participate.</p><p>This election, the clerk’s office will further strengthen the security of mail voting by deploying smart ballot drop boxes at all 56 of our early voting locations in suburban Cook County. Voters who do not wish to return their ballots through the U.S. Postal Service can drop their mail ballot at any one of these secure locations.</p><p>The boxes have built-in surveillance cameras, tamper-resistant construction and enhanced ballot tracking technology to provide voters with greater visibility into what happens after they deposit their ballot.</p><p>Most importantly, voters should not let the national debate over mail voting discourage them from exercising their rights. If you are eligible to vote in Illinois, you have the right to choose the voting method that works best for you, including voting by mail. Go to <a class="Link" href="http://www.cookcountyclerk.com/vote%20" target="_blank" >www.cookcountyclerk.com/vote </a>to review your voting options.</p><p>Our democracy depends not only on secure elections but on voters having confidence in those elections. We will continue doing everything in our power to earn that confidence, one secure ballot at a time.</p><p><i>Monica Gordon</i><b><i>, </i></b><i>Cook County clerk</i></p><h3>Eliminating microplastics</h3><p>A recent study by <a class="Link" href="https://environmentamerica.org/illinois/center/resources/microplastic-in-illinois/" target="_blank" ><u>Environment Illinois</u></a> found that 100% of the state's waterways — rivers, lakes, and streams — contained microplastics.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/microplastics.html" target="_blank" ><u>Microplastics</u></a> are such small pieces of plastic the tested locations look spotless to the naked eye. All the microplastic<u> </u>found in the Environment Illinois study contained tiny thread-like <a class="Link" href="https://oceanconservancy.org/blog/2024/08/27/difference-between-microplastics-microfibers/" target="_blank" ><u>fibers</u></a>. More than three-quarters of the microplastics found contained fragments and over half contained film.</p><p>These findings warrant urgent policy response. The non-biodegradable nature of plastic means microplastics never truly disappear; rather, they break down into progressively smaller pieces and accumulate within our environment. Four years ago, researchers found plastic in the digestive tracts of <a class="Link" href="https://pubs.acs.org/ascecg/article/10/43/14074/1494675/Microplastics-in-the-Great-Lakes-Environmental" target="_blank" >85% of fish</a> sampled from Lake Michigan tributaries — specifically the Milwaukee, St. Joseph and Muskegon rivers.</p><p>That threat isn’t limited to wildlife. <a class="Link" href="https://www.npr.org/sections/shots-health-news/2024/12/18/nx-s1-5227172/microplastics-plastic-nanoparticles-health-pfas" target="_blank" ><u>Studies</u></a> show microplastics have been detected in people's <a class="Link" href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35364151/" target="_blank" >lungs</a>, liver, <a class="Link" href="https://pubs.acs.org/doi/epdf/10.1021/acs.est.2c07179" target="_blank" >heart</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11406405/" target="_blank" >brain</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2024/05/22/1252831827/microplastics-testicles-humans-health" target="_blank" >testicles</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://hsc.unm.edu/news/2024/02/hsc-newsroom-post-microplastics.html" target="_blank" >placenta</a>.</p><p>In spite of the daunting problem, solutions exist. Illinois lawmakers should pass a statewide ban on unnecessary single-use plastics, close the loopholes that let plastic pellets spill into our waterways and require <a class="Link" href="https://abc7chicago.com/post/plastic-pollution-solution-washing-machine-filters-help-keep-millions-of-microfibers-out-drinking-water/14779305/" target="_blank" >microfiber-catching filters</a> on new washing machines. Producer-responsibility laws should also shift the cost of plastic waste onto companies that produce it — not on taxpayers.</p><p>Illinoisans deserve a clean environment. Policymakers must act now.</p><p><i>Renee Ma, senior, New Trier High School, Wilmette</i></p><h3>Trump can learn from Dolly</h3><p>When I reflect on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/08/25/dolly-parton-music-star-actor-and-beloved-figure-who-spanned-generations-has-died-at-80" >Dolly Parton</a>, I think of more than her triumphs in music, television and movies. I also think of the hundreds of million dollars in <a class="Link" href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/26/dolly-parton-philanthropy-charity-children-imagination-library" target="_blank" >charitable donations</a> she gave to assist with COVID-19 relief, natural disasters victims, hospitals, literacy programs and other humanitarian causes.</p><p>When President Donald Trump ordered all American flag to be flown in <a class="Link" href="https://thehill.com/blogs/in-the-know/6049911-dolly-parton-trump-flags-half-staff/" target="_blank" >half-staff </a>following Parton's death last week, I thought if he really wanted to honor her, he'd follow in her footsteps and donate some of his billions to charities he doesn't control.</p><p><i>Paul L. Newman, Merion Station, Pennsylvania</i></p><h3>Making lakes great again</h3><p>If Donald Trump actually wants to make the Great Lakes greater, he could start by releasing funds for preventing an invasive carp infestation.</p><p><i>John Powers, Rolling Meadows</i></p>

entries.title: Express eating disorder concern without body shaming
entries.summary: <p>You notice someone close to you has lost a lot of weight. You also notice that they’re skipping meals and talking more pessimistically about food and their body. You feel concerned but worry that <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/5-reasons-we-shouldnt-compliment-people-who-lose-weight-264696" target="_blank" >commenting on their body</a> might do more harm than good.</p><p>So what should you do? Where is the line between showing concern and being harmful?</p><p>I am familiar with the complexities and complications of eating disorders. As a <a class="Link" href="https://www.uwstout.edu/life-stout/dining/nutrition/contact-dietitian" target="_blank" >college campus dietitian</a>, I work together with students to confront their fears around food and dismantle the strict rules they might have around eating. My goal is to help students rediscover the joys of food and the social and cultural richness of eating with other people.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-2d0000" name="module-2d0000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Commentary bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Commentary</h2></div> </div><p>Despite my credentials in nutrition and psychology, my deepest understanding of eating disorders comes from my own personal experience with anorexia. I first started struggling with food when I was 13 and became visibly ill in high school, but it wasn’t until after my freshman year of college that I made substantial steps in my recovery journey. While eating disorders are often seen as a “teen problem,” there is <a class="Link" href="https://www.nationaleatingdisorders.org/eating-disorders-and-midlife-and-beyond/" target="_blank" >no age limit on eating disorders</a>. Adults with eating disorders may also have <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1176/appi.ps.20230193" target="_blank" >difficulty accessing appropriate support</a>.</p><p>Too often, I see the fear of saying the wrong thing turning into saying nothing at all, regardless of the <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/eating-disorders-are-the-most-lethal-mental-health-conditions-reconnecting-with-internal-body-sensations-can-help-reduce-self-harm-218079" target="_blank" >potential consequences of staying silent</a>. But empathy and respect can open the door to necessary conversations.</p><h3>When celebrities lose weight</h3><p>It can be jarring to see celebrities become suddenly, drastically thin.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://nypost.com/2025/12/10/lifestyle/hollywoods-new-ultra-thin-trend-is-dangerously-contagious/" target="_blank" >Ariana Grande, Cynthia Erivo and Meghan Trainor</a> are some celebrities whose bodies have become the topic of online discussion and speculation. But there are also examples of celebrities whose changes in appearance proved to be due to other health conditions. <a class="Link" href="https://www.businessinsider.com/chadwick-boseman-body-shaming-cancer-weight-loss-out-of-context-2020-9" target="_blank" >Chadwick Boseman</a> experienced significant weight loss while privately battling colon cancer, and <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/what-is-lupus-the-condition-selena-gomez-is-diagnosed-with-266273" target="_blank" >Selena Gomez</a> has spoken openly about how lupus and the medications she takes to treat it have affected her weight.</p><p>Discourse online often goes back and forth between fans expressing concern and others saying it’s none of their business and to leave them alone.</p><p>Knowing what to say or whether you should say anything at all can be incredibly confusing. Expressing concern is not inherently dangerous; it might help you process the shock of seeing your favorite celebrity dwindle before your eyes. Concurrently, commenting on someone else’s body on social media can do <a class="Link" href="https://healthcare.utah.edu/healthfeed/2025/08/what-body-shaming-and-how-does-it-impact-people" target="_blank" >real and serious harm</a>. Body-focused comments can lead to low self-esteem, depression, self-harm and may also contribute to eating disorders.</p><p>When I’m working with students, I choose my words carefully. I don’t start the conversation with “You have an eating disorder.” Rather, I listen closely, ask questions and respond with empathy. But there is a difference between choosing words carefully and choosing silence.</p><p>Avoiding talking about concerning changes to someone’s appearance because you’re afraid of saying the wrong thing risks normalizing concerning weight loss. This is especially the case for young adults who <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1111/1747-0080.12581" target="_blank" >look up to celebrities as role models</a>. Not talking about the consequences of life-threatening weight loss could unintentionally send a message that unhealthy levels of thinness is an ideal body type to aspire to.</p><h3>Eating disorders are on the rise</h3><p>At the height of my eating disorder, I remember thinking I was healthy. I was thinner than some popular celebrities at the time and had received so many compliments. How could something be wrong with how I look?</p><p>I wish I could say my experience is antiquated. But many young adults are asking themselves the same question today: What’s wrong with how they look? Silence becomes hard to defend when looking at the statistics. Eating disorders are on the rise, <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpeds.2023.113733" target="_blank" >doubling in prevalence worldwide</a> between 2000 and 2018. Rates continued to increase and <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2022-058198" target="_blank" >grow in severity</a> throughout the <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/eating-disorders-among-teens-have-more-than-doubled-during-the-covid-19-pandemic-heres-what-to-watch-for-201067" target="_blank" >COVID-19 pandemic</a>.</p><p>Eating disorders are not a phase someone can just “get over.” They are a <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/eating-disorders-are-the-most-lethal-mental-health-conditions-reconnecting-with-internal-body-sensations-can-help-reduce-self-harm-218079" target="_blank" >severe mental illness</a> with medical complications that can affect nearly every part of the body. Anorexia in particular has one of the <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1111/eat.70002" target="_blank" >highest death rates</a> of any eating disorder; patients face a roughly <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1002/eat.24223" target="_blank" >five times increased risk</a> of dying compared to the general population, particularly within the first 10 years after diagnosis.</p><p>Eating disorders don’t come in one shape.</p><p>Despite the risks, many people suffering from eating disorders may <a class="Link" href="https://www.eatingdisorderhope.com/blog/i-do-not-have-eating-disorder" target="_blank" >refuse to acknowledge the severity</a> of their illness and believe they are healthy. At the peak of my eating disorder I did not think I had a problem, despite being severely underweight. I grew up with magazines that had very similar messaging to what’s <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/mounting-research-documents-the-harmful-effects-of-social-media-use-on-mental-health-including-body-image-and-development-of-eating-disorders-206170" target="_blank" >seen on social media</a> today, telling people that they should suppress their hunger and be ashamed of their bodies. The message was that weight gain could mean the end of your social life.</p><p>Research has consistently shown that greater social media use is associated with <a class="Link" href="https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgph.0001091" target="_blank" >increased eating disorder symptoms</a>, particularly by encouraging body comparison and unrealistic body ideals. One study of nearly 1,800 young adults ages 19 to 32 found that those who spent the most time on social media had <a class="Link" href="http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jand.2016.03.021" target="_blank" >over double the risk</a> of having eating and body image concerns compared to those who spent the least time on social media.</p><p>Restrictive eating and other disordered eating behaviors can start to feel very normal when your whole algorithm is feeding you back-to-back tips on how to shrink yourself.</p><h3>How to talk to your loved one</h3><p>There is a fine line between commenting on someone’s body and expressing genuine concern for their health. So how do you start a conversation if you think someone you love has an eating disorder?</p><p>The first thing I recommend is <a class="Link" href="https://www.nationaleatingdisorders.org/warning-signs-and-symptoms/" target="_blank" >doing research on eating disorders</a> to learn the signs and symptoms. Know your facts and myths about nutrition and eating disorders. This background knowledge can help you gently reason with your loved one while avoiding unintentionally reinforcing the misinformation or <a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/all-foods-can-fit-in-a-balanced-diet-a-dietitian-explains-how-flexibility-can-be-healthier-than-dieting-270049" target="_blank" >diet culture</a> that could be contributing to their struggle.</p><p>When you feel it’s time to talk to your loved one, be prepared. You could be met with frustration, denial and annoyance. When my friends and family expressed concern, I huffed and rolled my eyes because I “didn’t have a problem.” It could take multiple tries before your loved one is ready for a conversation.</p><p>Then find a time and place to talk. Don’t do this during lunch, in front of many people or in the style of an intervention. Overwhelming your loved one could make them feel shame and shut down. A private conversation in a familiar place can make the conversation feel less intimidating, giving them the space to open up without putting them on the spot.</p><p>Use <a class="Link" href="https://www.verywellmind.com/what-are-feeling-statements-425163" target="_blank" >“I” statements</a>. This might sound like “I noticed you don’t get lunch with us anymore” or “I really care about you, and I am worried.” Using “you” statements can come off accusatory and make your loved one feel like they are being attacked.</p><p>Avoid giving simple solutions. One of the most common mistakes I see is people recommending that loved ones “just eat.” Eating disorders are <a class="Link" href="https://anad.org/eating-disorders-trauma-understanding-the-connection/" target="_blank" >much more complicated</a> than simply choosing not to eat. Giving simplistic solutions can minimize the internal conflict your loved one is going through and reduce your chances of talking with them again on this topic.</p><p>Finally, don’t push the conversation further if it’s short; leave it at that. Let your loved one approach you on their own terms. Sometimes sending texts that you are thinking of your loved one can show your support while still giving them space. While they might not tell you that they have an eating disorder, they may instead talk to you about other symptoms, such as anxiety. This could be the door to suggest that therapy could help.</p><h3>Progress over perfection</h3><p>The biggest key to having a successful conversation is compassion and patience with your loved one instead of pushing them. Progress over perfection is the golden rule I teach my students.</p><p>If your talk with your loved one doesn’t go the way you hoped it would, that doesn’t mean it was a failure. You still planted the message that you care about and are there for them. They may not be ready to acknowledge that they have a problem or seek help right away, but sometimes simply hearing someone show concern can be encouraging. Over time, the collective support of the people who love them can help them take that first step toward recovery.</p><p>Rather than asking whether you should say something, ask yourself how to discuss your concerns with empathy and understanding. The goal is not to force someone to admit they have a problem but to create a space for an honest and empathetic conversation.</p><p>A conversation that respectfully acknowledges that something may be wrong can remind the person you love that they do not have to face it alone.</p><p><i>Miranda Roberts is a dietitian at the University of Wisconsin-Stout Polytechnic.</i></p><p><i>This </i><a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/if-you-think-someone-has-an-eating-disorder-should-you-say-something-a-dietitian-explains-how-to-express-concern-without-body-shaming-289332" target="_blank" ><i>article</i></a><i> was originally published on </i><a class="Link" href="https://theconversation.com/us" target="_blank" ><i>theconversation.com</i></a></p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-000000" name="html-embed-module-000000"></a><iframe src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/289332/count.gif?distributor=republish-lightbox-advanced" width="1" height="1" style="border: none !important" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"></iframe> </div> </div><p></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-680000" name="module-680000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody">Send letters to <a class="Link" href="mailto:letters@suntimes.com" target="_blank" >letters@suntimes.com</a>. More about <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/submitting-opinion-and-letters" >how to submit here</a>.</div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: The Readers Have Spoken: The Bride Should Have Her Way
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I respectfully disagree with your response to "Woman's wedding has been hijacked." These mothers have no business trying to co-opt the bridal couple's wedding. If the daughter gives in, it's only the beginning of these two mothers trying to strong-arm themselves into trying to make future decisions for this poor couple.</p><p>The couple should put their feet down and tell these mothers to back off. It's their wedding, the only one (hopefully) they'll ever have, and, if they cave to these mothers' incipient narcissism at the expense of their wedding plans, they'll all regret it (including these mothers) for the rest of their lives. I'm truly surprised you didn't tell the couple to stand their ground. — <i>DON'T BACK DOWN</i></p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> Why should the bride put her hopes and dreams on the back burner just so the moms can impress their friends and associates? Not only does this advice fail to help the dad help his daughter, but it also sends the message to the daughter that her wedding is not really her wedding, it is a stage production the moms are orchestrating for their advantage. — <i>THINK AGAIN</i></p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> The advice for the hijacked wedding plans should have been for the bride to tell these two mothers to let the bride plan the wedding of her dreams, not theirs. I am assuming the bride can afford to pay for her small wedding. She can still include these mothers in something special. — <i>ONCE IN A LIFETIME</i></p><p><b>DEAR READERS:</b> In the first line of my response to Doting Dad, I agreed that the daughter should have the wedding she wants. In retrospect, it's clear I should have ended my answer there!</p><p>If one of the moms had written in to complain about the intimate wedding the bride had planned, I'm sure I would have told her in no uncertain terms to back off and let the bride have her way. My apologies to the couple for wavering and siding with those pushy moms. Thank you all for calling me out on this one!</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I've been ill for almost a year now. Before this, I was in perfect health, able to take care of all my own needs. I have no spouse or significant other. Before I got sick, I used delivery only for the rare pizza I didn't want to go out for. Now the only reason I have the food and medicine I need is because of delivery drivers. Thank you, delivery drivers! Bless you! I can't imagine what I'd do without you. I'm sorry if the tip isn't always the best. Please hang in there. You do more good than you will ever know. — <i>GRATEFUL IN WEST VIRGINIA</i></p><p><b>DEAR GRATEFUL:</b> Being a delivery driver can seem like a thankless job some of the time. I'm glad you do your best to show gratitude and tip them, and I hope their employers compensate them fairly. Not only do these workers serve the underserved, but they also help keep local businesses afloat.</p><p><i>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.</i></p>

entries.title: Review: Kokandy Productions’ ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ is a work of art
entries.summary: <p>Director Derek Van Barham and Kokandy Productions stage another Stephen Sondheim masterwork — following their much-praised “Sweeney Todd” and “Into the Woods” — in the cramped basement space of the Chopin Theatre. This time, it’s a richly emotional, cleverly designed and musically vivid “Sunday in the Park with George,” about the creation of painter Georges Seurat’s “A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte,” the large neo-impressionist masterpiece that — so very lucky for us! — hangs a few miles away in the Art Institute.</p><p>This show premiered in 1984 and earned Sondheim and his collaborator James Lapine the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, a rarity for a musical. That said, this show about art underappreciated in its time lost out to “La Cage aux Folles” for most of the Tony Awards, including Best Original Score; no offense to the immortal “I Am What I Am,” but this was, shall we say, a memorable error. And if you have any doubt about that, by all means catch this version, where music director Nick Sula, helped by a six-member orchestra and a startlingly effective sound design by Matt Reich, achieve at key moments a truly immersive swelling of Sondheim’s gorgeous songs, in which each note frequently represents a brush stroke, or rather a dot or dab in Seurat’s pointillist approach to painting, all adding up to something far bigger and evocative.</p><p>Anchored by two beautifully performed lead performances from Kevin Webb and Missy Wise Vanderzee, the show foregrounds the rich inner lives of the central characters, giving dimension to the external and internal conflicts that drive the highly fictionalized story. Act I follows George and his mistress and model Dot (see what the creators did there?!) as they bicker and ultimately split (“We Do Not Belong Together”), all while George works toward completing an oversized work that will never sell during his lifetime but will be recognized as revolutionary in the bigger picture.</p><div class="RatingCard Enhancement" data-module data-rating="4.0" data-align-center> <div class="RatingCard-title"> ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ </div> <div class="RatingCard-content"> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> </div> </div><p></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-d40000" name="module-d40000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><b>When:</b> Through Nov. 1<br><b>Where:</b> Chopin Theatre, 1543 W. Photo by Evan Hanover.jpg" srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1b6e376/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+95/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe8%2F52%2Fb05ea097464489e965461007a596%2Fsunday-in-the-park-7-photo-by-evan-hanover.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/faf0e7f/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+95/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe8%2F52%2Fb05ea097464489e965461007a596%2Fsunday-in-the-park-7-photo-by-evan-hanover.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1b6e376/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+95/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fe8%2F52%2Fb05ea097464489e965461007a596%2Fsunday-in-the-park-7-photo-by-evan-hanover.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Kevin Webb, Rachel Carreras, Lauren Miller and Danny Andrew Bennett star in Kokandy Productions’ revival of “Sunday in the Park with George.”</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Evan Hanover</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>George and Dot’s mutual attraction here comes across strongly, but so does their incompatibility. Webb’s George isn’t just obsessed with his art. Here, and uniquely in my experience, we can see that painting brings him an inner joy, a quality that makes the character’s choices far more sympathetic. Vanderzee, also highly compelling, brings her own specific take on Dot: firmly grounded, non-conformist in her own right, confident from the start in what she needs.</p><p>Notably, Van Barham finds a way to make Act II — which can feel like a whole different show — seem far more of a natural continuation, even after it skips forward a hundred years to a 1980s art museum. He infuses this often static second act with the same emotional detail and precision, just focused on an artist who fears his best work may be behind him.</p><p>Now Webb’s George is a modern artist playing with color and light — like his namesake ancestor before him — but this time using technology. His artistic rut, exacerbated by his need to please funders, finds great expression in Van Barham’s staging of “Putting It Together,” in which Webb seems constantly about to fall off the edge of the canvas/stage.</p><p>His elderly grandmother Marie (Vanderzee again as the daughter of Act I’s George and Dot and, again, very down-to-Earth, although now, amusingly, quirkily dotty) understands she needs to help him “Move On,” a number that here, as always, comes across as deeply affecting.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure A blank page or canvas.” In this version, with a set and lighting design by G “Max” Maxin IV, he describes the stage itself: a large, blank rectangular canvas, lying flat, raised a foot or so off the ground. As he summons the other characters who represent the ordinary visitors to a public Parisian park in the 1890s, George steps onto this canvas, which becomes the central playing area.</p><p>This is evocative in and of itself — emphasizing the ordering of chaos into art, and live theater as an art always in the process of creation. But the design concept also provides a giant payoff as Act I crescendos into its finale “Sunday.” Solving the problem that the confined space and in-the-round configuration don’t allow for a living re-creation of the Seurat painting, Van Barham finds a creative alternative to that and then amusingly begins Act II (“It’s Hot Up Here”) by stuffing nearly the entire cast of 14 onto that rectangular platform. </p><p>There are inconsistencies, unsurprising for a show with this size cast and variety of small subplots. But for every unfulfilled moment — the scenes involving the soldier, for example — there’s a surprisingly deep one, with a special call-out to actress Lauren Miller, so poignant as George’s nostalgic mother, who not only misremembers the past but laments the new construction she can see from her park bench. It will become the Eiffel Tower.</p>

entries.title: Boeing's image is deeply bruised, but the company's campaign money is still good with Illinois politicians
entries.summary: <p>Long headquartered in Chicago, the aerospace and defense contractor Boeing Co. has faced repeated allegations in recent years that it has put the pursuit of profits over passenger safety in building and designing aircraft — including the 737 MAX now criss-crossing the skies. </p><p>One of the jetliners crashed in 2018 shortly after taking off from an Indonesian airport, killing all 189 people aboard. In 2019, another 737 MAX went down in Ethiopia, killing all 157 on board. Boeing initially tried blaming the pilots. But it turned out a flawed system that can affect flight controls — and Boeing wasn’t truthful about with the Federal Aviation Administration or airlines — was a factor in both crashes.</p><p>Congressional hearings, a U.S. Justice Department investigation, a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission case, dozens of lawsuits in U.S. District Court in Chicago and two critical Netflix documentaries followed.</p><p>Boeing also stands to benefit financially from the war in Gaza through weapons production, according to published accounts and watchdog groups that accuse Israel’s military, a Boeing customer, of human rights abuses.</p><p>But none of that has stopped Illinois politicians from accepting campaign money from Boeing, with eight members of Congress from Illinois and northwest Indiana taking money from the company’s political action committee since the start of last year.</p><p>Three of them accepted $10,000 each, including U.S. Rep. Mike Quigley, a North Side Democrat running for Chicago mayor in next year’s election. He received four contributions in 2025 and four in 2026, according to Federal Election Commission records.</p><p>U.S. Rep. Mike Bost, a downstate Republican, accepted eight contributions from Boeing, two in 2026 and six last year, totaling $10,000.</p><p>U.S. Rep. Darin LaHood, a downstate Republican, accepted seven campaign contributions, all in 2025, totaling $10,000.</p><p>Those political figures either couldn’t be reached or wouldn’t comment. Boeing officials declined to comment.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-5e0000" entries.title: Temperatures could feel hotter than 100 degrees this week, forecasters say
entries.summary: <p>Some parts of the Chicago area could feel hotter than 100 degrees this week as a heat wave hits the area, forecasters say.</p><p>Chicago itself will likely be spared the hottest heat index — or how the temperature feels — of nearly 105 degrees, which is expected to hit the south suburbs on Tuesday and Wednesday.</p><p>Instead, Chicago could see temperatures climb into the 80s on Tuesday and into the lower 90s on Wednesday, according to Zachary Yack, meteorologist at the National Weather Service Romeoville office.</p><p>High humidity will push the heat index in Chicago into the low 90s on Tuesday and the upper 90s on Wednesday, he said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" entries.title: 1 man killed, 2 people injured after shooter fired shots into a crowd gathered in Douglas
entries.summary: <p>One man died and two others were injured when a shooter fired several times into a crowd late Saturday in the Douglas neighborhood, Chicago police said.</p><p>The crowd was gathered in the 100 block of East 37th Street when the shooting started around 11:20 p.m., according to police.</p><p>Three people were hit and taken to University of Chicago Medical Center, police said. </p><p>A 32-year-old man, shot several times, was in critical condition but later pronounced dead. He was identified as Antonio Hollis of Auburn Gresham, according to the Cook County medical examiner's office.</p><p>A 31-year-old man was also in critical condition, police said.. A 23-year-old woman, shot in her hand, was in good condition.</p>

entries.title: White Sox activate Tyler Schweitzer from paternity list in first of many roster moves this week
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON – A swap of left-handed relievers named Tyler on Monday morning kickstarted what should be a week full of roster shuffling for the American League Central-leading White Sox as they take on the Astros for a four-game series in Houston.</p><p>After missing this past weekend’s Twins series, <b>Tyler Schweitzer</b> was activated off the paternity list, taking the place of <b>Tyler Gilbert</b>. Having appeared in just five major league games this year, the 32-year-old Gilbert was the second reliever to appear in front of bulk pitcher <b>Jose Urquidy</b> in Sunday’s 5-1 loss to the Twins. Gilbert was charged with one run in 2 1/3 innings of work, but also allowed a first inning double to <b>Trevor Larnach</b> that plated two runners inherited from opener <b>Jordan Hicks</b>.</p><p>Schweitzer has posted a 3.64 ERA in 29 2/3 innings in the majors this year, filling a niche as a low-leverage long reliever in his rookie season; exemplified by him earning his first career save on June 30 for throwing the last four frames of a blowout victory in Baltimore.</p><p>“When a game goes and turns in a certain direction, I'm like, ‘All right, I need to start locking in,’” Schweitzer said. “I just call myself a reliever now, or honestly just a pitcher. Because whatever they need me to do, I'll do it, and that's what it's been. Going up and down is part of the business aspect of the game.”</p><p>By MLB rules, rosters can expand by two additional spots as the calendar turns to Sept. 1. The White Sox are set to add one pitcher and one position player, and already have pending moves of each variety nearing in the form of players returning from injury.</p><p>Recovered from a blister on his middle finger and coming off five scoreless innings in a Triple-A rehab start, <b>Davis Martin</b> is expected to be activated off the injured list on Wednesday to start against the Astros. Starting catcher <b>Kyle Teel</b> went 3-for-4 with a double on Sunday in his fourth rehab appearance with Triple-A Charlotte. He also caught all nine innings for the first time since suffering a left ankle sprain in July, and likely will also return sometime this week.</p><p>Having lost most of his season to hamstring, knee and ankle injuries, Teel has just a .589 OPS in 19 games with the White Sox. But after hitting .273/.375/.411 in 78 games as a rookie last year, he’s expected to provide the lineup a lift upon return…eventually.</p><p>“I'm telling him more than anything, this is kind of like your spring training all over again,” said Sox hitting director <b>Ryan Fuller.</b> “But he's feeling really good physically, and now it's getting up to speed and make sure those ABs are there.”</p>

entries.title: Alegaciones de que votarán los no ciudadanos impulsan ataques de Trump contra las elecciones intermedias
entries.summary: <p>El ritmo insistente del presidente Donald Trump y sus aliados sobre las supuestas amenazas de que personas que no son ciudadanas estadounidenses voten se ha intensificado a medida que se acerca la elección de noviembre.</p><p>Está presionando para que el Servicio Postal envíe boletas por correo sólo a <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/trump-mail-voting-supreme-court-157afc3c195ce0a62c522da5ce904b04" target="_blank" >votantes verificados como ciudadanos de Estados Unidos</a>. La Oficina del Censo promocionó <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/fact-check-trump-noncitizen-voting-census-bureau-36cf1524fda629b139b7de5c86119622" target="_blank" >un informe dudoso</a> sobre miles de personas no ciudadanas que habrían votado en 2020, una elección que el republicano perdió frente al demócrata Joe Biden.</p><p>El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) de Trump afirma, sin presentar pruebas, que hasta 250,000 personas no ciudadanas podrían estar en los padrones electorales en apenas cuatro estados.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-2a0000" name="module-2a0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Esta semana, el candidato republicano a gobernador de Maine <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/bobby-charles-audio-ice-polls-maine-governor-4e77e0f06a28d2a8f42b51ce28a91677" target="_blank" >confirmó una grabación de audio</a> en la que dijo que planea pedirle al zar fronterizo de Trump que envíe marshalls de Estados Unidos y agentes de la Oficina de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) a los centros de votación del estado para asegurarse de que solo los votantes legales emitan votos.</p><p>La portavoz de la Casa Blanca, Lauren Bis, dijo, al preguntársele sobre el informe del censo, que las pruebas de votación de personas no ciudadanas siguen “acumulándose”.</p><p>En realidad, el voto de personas que no son ciudadanas estadounidenses es <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/noncitizens-voting-republicans-election-2024-immigration-09b86e6768f755fd875f3c51b0e8ea70" target="_blank" >extremadamente raro</a> y se castiga como delito grave que puede llevar a la deportación. Aun así, los opositores afirman que la hiperconcentración en el tema por parte de Trump y sus aliados está preparando el terreno para impugnaciones legales de resultados que no le gusten en las elecciones intermedias, en las que está en juego el control del Congreso.</p><p>“Desechen estas afirmaciones engañosas y fraudulentas como excusa para [llevar a cabo] disturbios”, dijo Alexandra Chandler, directora de programas de impacto y de elecciones libres y justas del Democracy Project, una organización apartidista.</p><h3>La metodología del informe del censo es defectuosa, pero podría sembrar desconfianza</h3><p>El informe del censo, que el presidente citó en una publicación en Truth Social, señaló que en un “análisis inicial” encontró que 24,000 personas no ciudadanas votaron ilegalmente en 2020. Citó datos de un archivo de votantes comercial disponible, que se comparó con registros federales.</p><p>Los expertos dicen que la metodología podría haber creado falsos positivos. Por ejemplo, si el nombre de una persona se vinculó a la dirección incorrecta o si el estatus de ciudadanía de alguien no se había actualizado en una base de datos determinada.</p><p>Faltaban detalles que normalmente se incluirían en un informe de este tipo sobre tasas de error, dijo Justin Levitt, profesor de Derecho en la Loyola Marymount University. No obstante, los expertos en elecciones afirman que podría ayudar a generar desconfianza entre ciertos votantes en las elecciones generales de este año.</p><p>“Esto es una carpeta manila vacía que la administración agitará cuando diga que las elecciones fueron fraudulentas y que personas no ciudadanas votaron”, dijo Levitt.</p><h3>Responsables electorales desconcertados por la afirmación de 250,000 no ciudadanos en listas de registro de votantes</h3><p>La carta de julio del secretario de Seguridad Nacional, Markwayne Mullin, a California, Nevada, Nueva Jersey y Pensilvania, en la que alega que hasta casi 250,000 personas no ciudadanas estaban registradas en esos estados, fue recibida con escepticismo y solicitudes de más información.</p><p>“Tengo serias dudas sobre la fiabilidad de sus datos y la exactitud de sus afirmaciones, ya que mi oficina no ha compartido nuestra lista estatal de registro de votantes con DHS ni con ninguna otra agencia u funcionario federal”, dijo la secretaria del Estado de California, la demócrata Shirley Weber, en respuesta.</p><p>En Nueva Jersey, el departamento de Mullin indicó que hasta 35,000 personas no ciudadanas estaban registradas. Poco después de la carta, el estado, controlado por los demócratas, reveló que alrededor de <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/noncitizen-voter-registration-new-jersey-99ef57346bbe09ba2ff606538a76eede" target="_blank" >6,600 personas no ciudadanas fueron registradas indebidamente</a> a través de su sistema de vehículos motorizados en 2023 y 2024.</p><p>La demócrata gobernadora Mikie Sherrill dijo que esas personas respondieron “no” cuando se les preguntó si eran ciudadanas, pero aun así fueron registradas. La gobernadora dijo que su administración encontró que “menos de 400” de ellas habían votado y que ha comenzado a reemplazar al proveedor implicado en los registros indebidos.</p><p>El Secretario de Estado de Pensilvania, el republicano Al Schmidt, dijo en una carta esta semana que funcionarios del DHS reconocieron durante una reunión reciente que no tenían mucha confianza en que las 14,576 personas mencionadas en la carta inicial fueran en realidad no ciudadanas registradas indebidamente para votar.</p><p>Dijo que los funcionarios federales afirmaron que proporcionarían una metodología y que los funcionarios de Pensilvania estaban a la espera de esa información.</p><p>El Secretario de Estado de Nevada, Francisco Aguilar, demócrata, dijo que no entendía la metodología que usó el gobierno federal.</p><p>“Todo lo que puedo decir es que hemos hecho un trabajo significativo para asegurar que nuestras listas de registro estén lo más limpias posible”, dijo.</p><p>Los mensajes de la Associated Press buscando comentarios del DHS no fueron respondidos de inmediato.</p><h3>¿Endurecer la seguridad electoral o interferir en las elecciones intermedias?</h3><p>La atención implacable sobre las afirmaciones de que las personas no ciudadanas están empañando las elecciones en Estados Unidos llega mientras Trump sigue presionando a senadores republicanos para que <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/save-america-act-senate-recess-6dd2d8084ee42653b4db79cd565d1504" target="_blank" >aprueben un proyecto de ley</a> que les exigiría a las personas que muestren prueba documentada de ciudadanía cuando se registren para votar en las elecciones intermedias, pese a que millones de personas <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/save-act-documents-requirements-citizenship-voting-congress-dfb43bcdd0255d3665da588a60286b4e" target="_blank" >no tienen acceso fácil</a> a tales documentos.</p><p>El Safeguard American Voter Eligibility, o SAVE America Act, fue aprobado por la Cámara liderada por los republicanos, pero está estancado en el Senado, donde incluso algunos miembros del partido del presidente son escépticos sobre sus disposiciones.</p><p>Kathy Boockvar, exsecretaria de Estado demócrata de Pensilvania, que ahora dirige una firma no partidista de seguridad electoral, dijo que consideró la publicación del informe del censo por parte de la administración como parte de una estrategia de “hacer todo lo posible” para aprobar la legislación.</p><p>Los partidarios republicanos dicen que el proyecto de ley mejoraría la integridad de las elecciones, incluida la exigencia de mostrar una identificación con fotografía. Reunir los documentos necesarios para probar la ciudadanía sería difícil para muchos votantes potenciales. Un estudio de la Universidad de Maryland de 2025 estima que <a class="Link" href="https://cdce.umd.edu/sites/cdce.umd.edu/files/Who%20Lacks%20Documentary%20Proof%20of%20Citizenship%20March%202025.pdf" target="_blank" >21.3 millones de personas</a> en Estados Unidos que son elegibles para votar no tienen, o no tienen fácil acceso a documentos que comprueben su ciudadanía.</p><p>Los oponentes de Trump dicen que su sacar a relucir el espectro de que personas no ciudadanas voten, lo que llevaría a resultados fraudulentos, tiene menos que ver con mantener la integridad de las elecciones que con hacer todo lo posible para que su partido conserve el poder en Washington, D.C. después de noviembre.</p><p>El viernes, la fiscalía de Estados Unidos en Los Ángeles utilizó el arresto de un ciudadano hondureño acusado de registrarse fraudulentamente para votar como señal de que habrá más atención sobre el tema en California, un estado que tiene varias contiendas importantes para la Cámara de Representantes en noviembre.</p><p>El fiscal auxiliar Bill Essayli dijo que el arresto fue “el primero de muchos por venir” mientras advertía que “no se puede saber cuántas personas no ciudadanas están actualmente registradas para votar” en el estado.</p><p>“Trump está tratando de preparar el terreno para rechazar las elecciones del ’26”, dijo la Secretaria de Estado de Colorado, la demócrata Jena Griswold. “Está tratando de desestabilizar tanto la confianza como la administración real de las elecciones. Sus esfuerzos por desestabilizar la información y la administración electoral no están funcionando”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Man forced into Lake View home, shot in neck
entries.summary: <p>A man was seriously wounded Sunday night when another man forced him into a Lake View home at gunpoint and shot him in the neck, Chicago police said.</p><p>The man, 33, told officers he was forced by the attacker into the home just after 7:30 p.m. in the 3600 block of North Pine Grove Avenue, according to police. The arracker then shot him in his neck inside the home. He was taken to Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center in serious condition. </p><p>No one has been arrested, according to police. </p>
